newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks snap back from losses, end firmer.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks snap back from losses, end firmer.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur shares bounced back from a one-day bout of profit-taking as buying in lower-tier main board stocks and small-capitalisation issues helped the market finish firmer, dealers said. "There was also follow-through from Wall Street," said Ami Moris, a vice president in dealing at CapitalCorp. "It's very much the second- and third-liners and the Second Board is holding very well." The Dow rose 78.50 to 7,067.46 on Tuesday.
At day's end, the Composite Index of 100 large stocks stood at 1,258.64, up 10.74 points. The Second Board index jumped 9.26 points or 1.45 percent to 649.18.
Market volume was 521 million shares, against 447 million on Tuesday. Main board turnover accounted for 458 million of the total, with gainers topping losers by 504 to 112.
The broad EMAS index ended up 3.84 points or 1.06 percent to 366.04.

"Locals have been in the market but not in a big way," said an institutional dealer with a bank-linked brokerage firm. He said some investors may be sidelined for the time being to monitor reports on Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping's health.
When he dies, "there will be a short domino effect in the region (markets)," the dealer said.
